title: Table format
description: What a schema becomes on its way to being read. Two halves kept apart: doc is what a page shows a person, rules is the residue needed to rebuild something that validates the same documents. A renderer may read doc and must never read rules.

title.description: What the whole document is called.

dialect.description: Which JSON Schema dialect this came from. Kept so the rebuilt schema can declare the same one.

source.description: Where the original was read from.

root.description: What a whole file looks like, as opposed to any named shape inside it.

shapes.description: Every named shape, most used first, because what everything else is built on is what a reader needs first.

dropped.description: Rules in the original that have no honest short reading. Listing them is what stops a page quietly claiming to be complete.

containers.description: Keywords belonging to a drawer that holds shapes but is not itself a shape. Part of the rules half: never read by a renderer.

id.description: The pointer this shape sits at in the original. Links use it, and the rebuild uses it to put the shape back where it came from.

group.description: The drawer it was filed under, when the original filed shapes in drawers.

usedBy.description: How many places point at this shape. This is what the ordering is built on.

isList.description: True when the shape is itself a list. Its rows then describe one entry, not the shape.

example.description: One real value written by the schema's author. Carried to every field pointing here, so a reader is not sent away to find out what to type.

picks.description: One field whose value decides which shape applies. Thirty if-then blocks saying the same thing are one decision, not thirty rules.

rules.description: The validating residue. Never read by a renderer.

exclusiveSets.description: Same, at the level of a whole shape.

name.description: A field's name is not always a name. It may be one the writer chooses, or one that only has to look a certain way.

text.description: What to show. For a pattern, what the pattern allows, said in words.

pattern.description: The pattern itself, for the rebuild.

borrowed.description: This field comes from a shape this one inherits. It applies here, but it is declared elsewhere, and writing it back on the rebuild would move the rule.

from.description: Which shape it was borrowed from.

brings.description: Filling this field in makes other things needed. Fires on the field being present, whatever its value.

rules.description: The validating residue for this field. Never read by a renderer.

value.description: What goes in a field, said as a fact rather than as a way of drawing it. A bar, a set of chips and a yes or no toggle are three ways to draw one idea, and choosing between them is the renderer's job, not this format's.

words.description: The plainest true sentence about this value.

refs.description: The shapes it may be any one of.

href.description: Rules kept in another file, and where.

alsoFollowsRef.description: A shape whose rules apply on top of these. A pointer beside other keywords is inheritance, not replacement. Only the pointer is stored; the name is looked up.

item.description: What one entry of a list holds.

itemClosed.description: A list is closed on its entries, not on itself.

options.description: Forms this value may take, when they are not all named shapes.

forbidden.description: Values that are not allowed. Only kept where it is a plain exclusion, because a negated shape has no short honest reading.

default.description: What it means to leave the field out.

example.description: A real value from the author. This is what tells alternatives apart when they differ only by format.

patternWords.description: What a pattern allows, said in words, because the pattern itself is unreadable.

range.description: Two ends and what they count. Drawn rather than written, wherever the renderer can.

nullable.description: The value itself may be empty.

exclusiveSets.description: Groups of fields that cannot all be used at once. The commonest real use of a negation, and a rule a writer will otherwise trip over.

slots.description: Entries at fixed positions: the first is one thing, the second another.

restItem.description: What every entry after the fixed slots holds. Separate from `item`, because a list can have both fixed slots and a rule for the rest.

slotsOnly.description: The list stops after its fixed slots. Nothing may follow them.

thenRequires.description: Fields that become required when the condition holds. A branch can make an existing field required without adding any fields of its own.

elseRequires.description: The same, for when the condition does not hold.

howManyFields.description: How many fields a group must have. A rule a writer can break, so it belongs on the page.

whoWrites.description: Whether the reader fills this in or only receives it.

holds.description: What the text inside a field actually is, when it carries something other than plain text.
